citation.authors: Vislocky LM, Gaine PC, Pikosky MA, et al.
citation.title: Gender impacts the post-exercise substrate and endocrine response in trained runners
citation.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

population.description: Six trained men and six trained women, runners: 'a mix of collegiate runners and serious recreational athletes'. Enrolment: aged 18-30 y, running >= 56 km/wk, VO2peak > 45 (women) and > 50 (men) mL/kg/min, matched on training volume and fitness; no resistance training during or for a month before. Printed weekly running: men 51 +/- 4 and women 37 +/- 1 miles/wk (Discussion); men ran about 14 more miles/wk (P < 0.05). Screened by medical history (no metabolic or cardiovascular abnormality, no gastrointestinal disorder, no supplements or anabolic steroids; women eumenorrheic, not on oral contraceptives, studied in the early follicular phase, days 1-7, estradiol 39.2 +/- 3.6 pg/mL). The model carries no training status, so these are endurance-trained people, not an average healthy adult; the men and women were two independent studies with identical conditions. Age and BMI are given per sex in the protocol arms (Table 1, mean +/- SEM, n = 6, SD computed as SEM x sqrt(6)); the paper gives no observed ranges.

protocols.name: rest_female
protocols.description: female runners at rest: baseline (REST) blood sample after a 10-12 h overnight fast, before the 75 min run (run not entered) Arrival ~0600 h after a 10-12 h overnight fast; a catheter was inserted into an antecubital vein and the baseline (REST) sample drawn after that (no rest period or exact clock time of the draw is stated; venous, lithium-heparin/EDTA plasma). Before it: 8 days of provided eucaloric diet (1.8 g/kg/d protein, 30% fat, remainder carbohydrate; training and competing continued) and no exercise the day before (~36 h).; a 30-minute fasted run-in stands for the single sample (arm ends there). prefast_hours 10 is the lower end of the stated 10-12 h. Age and BMI SEs from Table 1 converted to SD = SE x sqrt(6): age 22.7 +/- 0.7 SE -> 1.71; BMI 22.9 +/- 1.6 SE -> 3.92.

protocols.name: rest_male
protocols.description: male runners at rest: baseline (REST) blood sample after a 10-12 h overnight fast, before the 75 min run (run not entered) Arrival ~0600 h after a 10-12 h overnight fast; a catheter was inserted into an antecubital vein and the baseline (REST) sample drawn after that (no rest period or exact clock time of the draw is stated; venous, lithium-heparin/EDTA plasma). Before it: 8 days of provided eucaloric diet (1.8 g/kg/d protein, 30% fat, remainder carbohydrate; training and competing continued) and no exercise the day before (~36 h).; a 30-minute fasted run-in stands for the single sample (arm ends there). prefast_hours 10 is the lower end of the stated 10-12 h. Age and BMI SEs from Table 1 converted to SD = SE x sqrt(6): age 20.6 +/- 0.6 SE -> 1.47; BMI 21.6 +/- 0.4 SE -> 0.98.

Cortisol at REST, POST+30, POST+210 (Results, Cortisol): means labelled nmol/L, changes labelled ng/mL; the male change (-95.7) equals the difference of the nmol/L means (375.3 - 471.0) but the female change (+210.3) does not (889.7 - 661.6 = 228.1), so the unit label and the arithmetic disagree and the unit cannot be settled
